regions.title: MoE combine: post-all-to-all concat + score multiply + bf16 cast + deterministic scatter-add
regions.fusion_kind: gather/segmented-reduction (scatter-add) with pointwise prologue; copy elimination
regions.shapes_dtypes: routed_output [786432,7168] bf16 (a2a output chunks) * scores [786432,1] fp32 -> fp32 [786432,7168] -> bf16; scatter-add by token index [786432] int64 into zeros [98304,7168] bf16
regions.bitwise_notes: Product is computed in fp32 and rounded to bf16 per row (keep); each output row is the sum of top_k=8 bf16 rows accumulated by the deterministic sort-based index_put (stable sort by token, fp32 accumulation, one bf16 rounding). A gather-based segmented reduction per token must use the same contribution order (expert-sorted position order) and the same accumulation dtype. The concat is pure data movement.
regions.blockers: The all-to-all boundary sits before the region (real EP); reading per-rank chunks needs spmd_types _AllToAllUneven to expose them or an all_to_all_single into a caller buffer. Deterministic mode forces sort-based index_put. Under full remat this whole span is replayed in recompute only to re-capture saved inputs of the multiply and the scatter-add index; its outputs are dead there.
regions.how_found: op table: largest memory-bound class (aten::mul at token_dispatcher.py:155, 21.4 ms/layer); ET dataflow component mul -> copy_ -> index_put; source review of _score_and_scatter_add
regions.notes: Dataflow: the all-to-all output chunks are concatenated, multiplied row-wise by the score (fp32 product, 22.5 GB), cast to bf16 (11.3 GB) and scatter-added into a zero [98304,7168] buffer; every intermediate has a single consumer inside the span, so one kernel can read each routed row once and write each token row once. Recompute instances (58 of 116, ~2846 ms) produce dead outputs: torch_remat replays the span only because the multiply and the scatter-add save tensors; a combine op whose saved inputs are already persisted would skip it entirely (remat-policy change, not fusion; not counted in the gap). A non-bitwise variant could scatter into the shared-expert output instead of zeros (removes zeros + shared_add) but changes the summation order. Fusing the score multiply into the w2 grouped-GEMM epilogue before the all-to-all is T3 and also changes rounding order.

regions.title: MoE combine backward: scatter-add grad gather + score-multiply backward (dgrad, score grad reduction)
regions.shapes_dtypes: grad_out [98304,7168] bf16 gathered to [786432,7168]; bf16->fp32 grad; *scores fp32; *routed_output fp32 then sum over 7168 -> score grad [786432] fp32; fp32 -> bf16 routed grad
regions.bitwise_notes: Gather and casts are exact; the routed-output grad is fp32 grad*score rounded to bf16 (pointwise). The score grad is a 7168-wide fp32 row sum: the fused kernel must reproduce aten's sum reduction tree.
regions.blockers: Autograd splits this into GatherBackward / ToCopyBackward / MulBackward nodes; a fused version needs a custom autograd op for the whole combine. The all-to-all backward follows immediately.
regions.how_found: op table backward rows linked by autograd sequence number to the combine forward ops; source review
regions.notes: Dataflow: grad_out [98304,7168] is gathered to routed order, upcast, multiplied by the score (routed grad, cast to bf16) and by the saved routed output (row-summed into the score grad); all intermediates are single-consumer; external inputs are grad_out, routed_output, scores, indices. Pair of E-01 (combine_fwd).

regions.bitwise_notes: Each token row sums 8 bf16 rows in the deterministic sort order with fp32 accumulation; must match exactly.
regions.blockers: Collective boundary before; IndexBackward materializes zeros; deterministic mode.
regions.how_found: op table backward rows linked by seq_id to the local reorder gathers
regions.notes: Dataflow: the all-to-all-backward chunks are concatenated and scatter-added (8 rows per token) into a zero [98304,7168] buffer; the zeros and the concat are consumed only by the index_put. The InputBuffer add that follows (routed grad + shared-expert grad) is in E-17 (ffn_norm_bwd_accum).

regions.title: MoE permute backward: zeros + deterministic index_put accumulate over a permutation
regions.shapes_dtypes: zeros [786432,7168] bf16; index_put_(accumulate=True) of grad [786432,7168] bf16 by permuted_indices
regions.bitwise_notes: Indices form a permutation, so each element is 0 + g computed in fp32 and rounded: equal to g except that -0.0 becomes +0.0. A gather by the inverse permutation must add +0.0 to match.
regions.blockers: IndexBackward always materializes zeros and accumulates; replacing it needs a custom autograd op that knows the indices are a permutation.
regions.how_found: op table backward rows (largest backward index_put); seq_id link to _permute
regions.notes: Dataflow: IndexBackward zero-fills [786432,7168] and accumulates the w13-input grad through permuted_indices; the zero buffer has no other consumer and the indices are a permutation.

regions.title: Routed-expert SwiGLU recompute + backward in one pass (h for the w2 weight grad and d_gate_up from one read of gate_up)
regions.shapes_dtypes: recompute: gate_up [786432,2,2048] -> h [786432,2048]; backward: d_h + gate_up -> d_gate_up [786432,2,2048] bf16
regions.bitwise_notes: Pointwise; the fused kernel must round silu(gate) to bf16 where eager saved it, and evaluate silu_backward with aten's fp32 formula (FMA contraction must match).
regions.blockers: Autograd node boundaries (MulBackward0, SiluBackward0, UnbindBackward0). The one-pass form also needs torch_remat to stop replaying the activation (it replays the whole block before the block's backward) and the w2 grouped-GEMM backward to run dgrad before the activation kernel and wgrad after it (one node today).
regions.how_found: op table backward rows linked to activation.py by seq_id; recompute-to-backward edges (rc_to_bwd) from the silu/mul replay to the mul backward
regions.notes: Dataflow: the recompute reads gate_up and writes h (consumed only by the w2 weight-grad GEMM); the backward reads d_h, gate_up and the saved silu output and writes d_gate_up through two muls, silu_backward and a stack; gate_up is read by both phases and every intermediate is single-consumer. Fallback without reordering: one fused recompute kernel + one fused backward kernel, ideal 1339 + 2232 = 3571 us per layer (vs 2678 us one-pass).

regions.title: MoE unpermute (expert-major -> rank-major) as deterministic index_put scatter
regions.shapes_dtypes: out[permuted_indices,:] = routed_output, [786432,7168] bf16, permuted_indices [786432] int64
regions.bitwise_notes: permuted_indices is a permutation (no duplicates), so a gather by the inverse permutation (or a plain scatter) writes identical bits; only the bounds checks of index_put are extra.
regions.blockers: Deterministic mode routes index_put through the sort-based kernel even without accumulation. The output feeds the combine all-to-all, so fusion with the combine is blocked by the collective; fusion with the w2 grouped GEMM epilogue would be T3.
regions.how_found: op table: aten::_index_put_impl_ at token_dispatcher.py:569 at 3.4x its roofline; source review

regions.title: Query RoPE (bf16->fp32 strided copy, complex multiply, fp32->bf16) + concat with q_nope
regions.bitwise_notes: Complex multiply in fp32 (re = ac - bd, im = ad + bc) then round to bf16; FMA contraction must match aten's complex mul kernel.

no_opportunity.what: FSDP2 all-gather copy-in / copy-out and reduce-scatter packing (_foreach_copy_, split_with_sizes_copy, chunk_cat, chunk_cat_mixed_dtype, cat)
no_opportunity.reason: Owned by FSDP2's flat-buffer protocol around real collectives; the copies remain with NCCL. Fusing them means changing FSDP (all-gather into parameter storage, reduce-scatter from strided grads), not model code. With the fake process group the neighbouring collective is itself a copy, so no fusion can be judged.
